newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-W.INDIES WILTS BEFORE TEA ON FIRST DAY V AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-W.INDIES WILTS BEFORE TEA ON FIRST DAY V AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Australian legspinners Michael Bevan and Shane Warne grabbed seven wickets between them to demolish the West Indies' batting lineup before tea on the first day of their fourth test match on Saturday.
Left armed legspinner Bevan took four wickets in a startling 28 ball spell that utterly mesmerised a tentative and distracted West Indies middle and lower order.
West Indies capitulated to be all out for 130 just over an hour after the lunch break, having gone to lunch at 82 for five on what was generally seen as a good batting pitch.
This is the West Indies second lowest total against Australia at the Adelaide Oval since 1951/52, when they scored 105. It is their fourth batting collapse in a row on this tour.
Australia made a solid start to their first innings and were 29 for no wicket at tea against a depleted West Indies pace attack.
Bevan, in his first match as a recognised bowler, finished with four for 31.
He has previously played as a batsman who bowled occasionally, but was selected for this match as a second spinner after a dramatic improvement this season.
The 26 year old had started poorly, bowling too full and wide to the West Indies top order who were only too happy to drive him to the boundary.
But once he found a good length, the West Indies just could not cope with his bouncy leg-spinners that approach medium pace on occasion.

Warne was also in destructive form, taking the prize wicket of an in-form Brian Lara before lunch with his first ball to the left-hander, delighting a capacity crowd of over 20,000 at the tree-lined and sun-drenched Adelaide Oval.
Warne took two wickets for seven runs in his first two overs, including that of Chivnarine Chanderpaul who has been the West Indies' most consistent batsman on tour.
The West Indies are expected to struggle to dismiss Australia cheaply on a pitch settling into a good batting wicket.

Strike fast bowler Curtly Ambrose, the chief destroyer for the West Indies in their third test win in Melbourne, was forced to withdraw at the last minute after failing a morning fitness test with a strained groin.
The West Indies have also lost paceman Kenny Benjamin, who returned earlier this month with a side strain.
Ambrose and Benjamin have been replaced by Cameron Cuffy and Patterson Thompson, who have three test matches of experience between them.

Australia lead the five test series 2-1 and only need to draw or win this match to retain the Frank Worrell Trophy, which they won in 1995 in the Caribbean when they were the first team to beat the West Indies in a test series for 15 years.
